title: Assembly
summary: The whole base in the drill hall: the anthem, the charter, and the Deputy Director's address with its two rules. Then Vetch collects Section Nine.
goal: They have heard the Deputy Director's address, seen the staff on the platform, and met their section officer, Vetch.
howToPlay: Ceremonial and sincere: nobody in this room is lying. Read the address as a real speech. **Make sure the two rules land: curfew is small, a refused order is not.**

intro.where: The drill hall. Section Nine sits together at the front; their cards say so.
intro.readAloud: The drill hall smells of floor polish and four hundred people: the whole base has turned out, and the forty of you in the new intake have the front rows. Along the platform, a dozen staff in a dozen different uniforms stand in a line. Above them, in a heavy frame, hangs the founding charter, and somebody has polished the glass.
intro.landmark: The charter, framed over the platform.

position.note: Section Nine together among the intake's chairs.

cast.label: Deputy Director Takamine
cast.role: Deputy Director, one rung below the top.

brief.wants: This intake to understand what it has joined, and to take it as seriously as he does.
brief.opensWith: Nothing: he waits, without a word, until the room goes quiet on its own.

willDiscuss.note: "To be ready. Everything else is how."
Lessons in the morning, and afternoons theirs to choose once their section officer releases them.
"Curfew is a small thing. An order is not."
"You'd sit in my office, I'd ask you why, and I'd listen."

willNotDiscuss.topic: Why the Directorate came to Kurose
willNotDiscuss.why: He means it kindly: "The founders' reasons are the founders' to give."

willNotDiscuss.topic: Why the intake was brought forward
willNotDiscuss.why: "The date moved. Dates do, here. I'm sorry it cost some of you a fortnight at home."
"Medical's business. Ask Doctor Mordant, and good luck to you."
"You'll meet them soon enough. Not today."

voice.register: Measured and warm. Pauses before the parts he cares about.
samples: "You will be asked to do things that seem beneath you. Some of them are. Do them anyway, and then come and tell me which ones."
"Good question. I don't know. Find out, and tell me."

brief.statblock: Proposed: level 8, a senior officer, non-combat. Perception DC 26, Will DC 29, Deception DC 26.

brief.wants: To be seen with the senior staff, and to start Section Nine's day his way.
brief.opensWith: "Section Nine. With me. Yes, all of you."

willDiscuss.note: "First period, then the stores, then second period. It's on the sheet. Read the sheet."

willNotDiscuss.why: He doesn't know, and won't say so: "Sections are assigned work. That is what a section is."

voice.register: Clipped and procedural. Never wrong in his own account: surprised, he pauses one beat, then says it was the plan.
samples: "Section Officer Vetch. You'll address me as Section Officer."

brief.statblock: Proposed: level 3, an officer, non-combat. Perception DC 19, Will DC 19, Deception DC 19. Striking him ends in a hearing, not a fight.

brief.wants: To get back to his clinic.

cast.label: Hulda Brack
cast.role: Head of the machine shop, on the platform.

brief.wants: To be back on her shop floor, where things make sense.

voice.register: One laugh, much louder than the room allows, cut off halfway.

cast.label: The comms officer
cast.role: The radio voice off the plot room, on the platform.

brief.wants: To see who this year's intake are.

voice.register: She watches the intake, not the speaker.

beats.text: Everyone stands for the anthem. Read it, then wait to hear what each character does.
beats.readAloud: A piano starts, and four hundred people stand. The anthem is old and slow, and everyone in the room over thirty knows every word without looking.
beats.note: If a player says what their character does: Offer the check to get through a song they don't know.

beats.text: The Deputy Director gives the address. Read it as a speech. Short on time, cut any paragraph but the last two. <trig id="deputy-director-steps-up"/> <trig id="enrolment-instructions"/>
beats.readAloud:
My name is Seiichi Takamine. It will be on a great many documents you sign this year, so you may as well hear it said once, by me.

You have joined Tokubetsu Taisaku Honbu, the Special Countermeasures Headquarters, which this city calls the Directorate. We exist to be ready. We keep the sirens, the shelters and the drills, and on most days we keep the harbour, the drains and the heavy lifting this city can't do without. In a hundred and fifty years the alarm has never once been real. That is a promise, and it is not a guarantee.

You will find we are two things at once. We are a school, so you will sit lessons. We are a service, so you will drill, carry orders and stand watches. In the mornings you will be taught. In the afternoons, once your section officer releases you, the time is yours: the gymnasium, the range, the library, or a lesson you choose yourselves. Spend it well. Nobody here will spend it for you.

We have a great many rules, and you will break most of them by accident before the month is out. Two you should know today. If you are out after curfew, that is a small thing: it will be written down, and you will be told off. If you are given a direct order and you refuse it, that is not a small thing. It is the most serious thing you can do here, and you will explain yourself to someone like me.

That is all. Your section officers have your postings. Welcome to the Directorate. I am glad you are here.
beats.note: Do: Afterwards he takes questions, and answers plainly.

beats.text: If anyone watches the platform instead of the speaker, offer the check.
beats.note:
If anyone asks who that is: Vetch, without looking round: "Administration. Eyes front."
Secret: It's Rupiah, a founder, high in the administration, here to watch and not be involved. Nobody stares at a founder; it's manners.

beats.text: If anyone looks closely at the charter, offer the check to read its four signatures.
beats.note: Secret: The doctor's scrawl is Shucks's own hand from before his right hand came off. Rand still writes in it.

beats.text: Vetch collects Section Nine at the door and gives them the day's timetable. <trig id="vetch-collects"/>
beats.readAloud: "Section Nine. With me. Yes, all of you." He doesn't wait to see if you follow. "Section Officer Vetch. First period, then the stores, then second period. It's on the sheet. Read the sheet."

outro.endsWhen: Vetch has led Section Nine out of the hall.

transition.line: "First period. School block. Don't be late."

writeDown: Who caught the Deputy Director's name.
Who read the charter, and who watched the platform.

position.note: Leaving with Vetch for the school block.

temptations.text: When the Deputy Director says they'll break most rules by accident, Hulda Brack's laugh goes off like a dropped spanner and stops halfway. He waits for silence, and the two rules land harder.
Section Nine's row is one chair short. Someone stands, shares or goes looking, and if the Deputy Director notices from the platform, he apologises for the chair before he says another word.

reactionPrompts.text: The two rules registering with the table.
Section Nine's first impression of Vetch.

notes: Everyone on the platform is someone they'll deal with: Shucks, Hulda Brack, Vetch and the Comms Officer, and at the far end Rupiah, whom nobody looks at. The address makes the Directorate a school and a service at once, gives the candidates their afternoons, and states the two rules. It names no founder and gives no reason for Kurose.
